assignments.text:
There are people who talk of
themselves, and think of themselves, as it were, under protest, and with
depreciation, not actually able to convince themselves that anybody
cares; but Lucilla, for her part, had the calmest and most profound
conviction that, when she discussed her own doings and plans and
clevernesses, she was bringing forward the subject most interesting to
her audience as well as to herself. Such a conviction is never without
its fruits.
assignments.summary: Lucilla's complete conviction in her own importance is the source of her persuasiveness; she genuinely believes her interests are everyone's interests.
assignments.best_quote: Lucilla, for her part, had the calmest and most profound conviction that, when she discussed her own doings and plans and clevernesses, she was bringing forward the subject most interesting to her audience as well as to herself

assignments.text:
Nothing, indeed, could have come more
opportunely for Lucilla, who possessed in perfection that faculty of
throwing herself into the future, and anticipating the difficulties of a
position, which is so valuable to all who aspire to be leaders of
mankind.
assignments.summary: Lucilla possesses the valuable ability to anticipate difficulties and plan ahead, a trait essential for leadership.
assignments.best_quote: that faculty of throwing herself into the future, and anticipating the difficulties of a position, which is so valuable to all who aspire to be leaders of mankind

assignments.text:
When you add to a man capable of giving excellent dinners,
like Dr Marjoribanks, another man like young Mr Cavendish, Mrs
Woodburn's brother, who was a wit and a man of fashion, and belonged to
one of the best clubs in town, and brought down gossip with the bloom on
it to Grange Lane; and when you join to Mrs Centum, who was always so
good and so much out of temper that it was safe to calculate on
something amusing from her, the languid but trenchant humour of Mrs
Woodburn—not to speak of their husbands, who were perfectly available
for the background, and all the nephews and cousins and grand-children,
who constantly paid visits to old Mr Western and Colonel Chiley; and the
Browns, when they were at home, with their floating suite of admirers;
and the young ladies who sang, and the young ladies who sketched, and
the men who went out with the hounds, when business permitted them; and
the people who came about the town when there was an election; and the
barristers who made the circuit; and the gay people who came to the
races; not to speak of the varying chances of curates, who could talk or
play the piano, with which Mr Bury favoured his parishioners—for he
changed his curates very often; and the occasional visits of the lesser
county people, and the country clergymen;—it will be plainly apparent
that all that was wanting to Carlingford was a master-hand to blend
these different elements.
assignments.summary: The narrator catalogs Carlingford's abundant social assets—excellent dinners, witty figures, entertaining women, visiting relatives, local events, clergy, and county visitors—requiring only masterful coordination.
assignments.best_quote: all that was wanting to Carlingford was a master-hand to blend these different elements

assignments.text:
And Lucilla knew it just as well as they
did, which gave a certain sense of condescension and superiority to her
frankness. "I never pretend I don't try to please them," Miss
Marjoribanks said; and the matrons found themselves worsted as usual;
for, to be sure, it was not for  Them , but for the good of the
community in general, that Lucilla exerted herself so successfully.
assignments.summary: Lucilla frankly states she makes no pretence of not trying to please gentlemen, leaving the matrons defeated, as her efforts serve community good rather than personal interest.
assignments.best_quote: I never pretend I don't try to please them

assignments.text:
People who like to discover the alloy which blends
with all human motives, may suppose that Lucilla felt her own credit as
the leader of society at stake, and would not admit that she had been
duped. But this had in reality but a very small share in the matter.
assignments.summary: While others might suppose Lucilla's self-interest drives her actions, Oliphant asserts that reputation concerns play only a minor role in her character.
assignments.best_quote: People who like to discover the alloy which blends with all human motives, may suppose that Lucilla felt her own credit as the leader of society at stake, and would not admit that she had been duped. But this had in reality but a very small share in the matter.

assignments.text:
Policy had been constantly inspired and backed by nature in
the measures Lucilla had taken for the organisation and welfare of her
kingdom, and even what people took for the cleverest calculation was in
reality a succession of happy instincts, by means of which, with the
sovereignty of true genius, Miss Marjoribanks managed to please
everybody by having her own way.
assignments.summary: Lucilla's success derives not from cold calculation but from happy instincts and true genius that blend policy with natural feeling.
assignments.best_quote: Policy had been constantly inspired and backed by nature in the measures Lucilla had taken for the organisation and welfare of her kingdom

assignments.text:
Lucilla
was not blind to the dangers that surrounded her, nor indifferent to the
partial disappointment she had undergone; but she saw that, in spite of
all, her great work was making progress. And when we announce that Miss
Marjoribanks herself was satisfied, there remains little more to say.
assignments.summary: Despite obstacles and disappointments, Lucilla recognizes that her great social work is advancing, and her satisfaction indicates victory.
assignments.best_quote: Lucilla was not blind to the dangers that surrounded her, nor indifferent to the partial disappointment she had undergone; but she saw that, in spite of all, her great work was making progress. And when we announce that Miss Marjoribanks herself was satisfied, there remains little more to say.

assignments.text:
She paused a moment in the
accompaniment to clap her hands after that strophe was accomplished, and
then resumed with energy. For, to be sure, she knew by instinct what
sort of clay the people were made of by whom she had to work, and gave
them their reward with that liberality and discrimination which is the
glory of enlightened despotism. Miss Marjoribanks was naturally elated
when she had performed this important and successful  tour .
assignments.summary: Lucilla pauses to applaud Barbara's performance, understanding instinctively how to motivate people and dispense rewards with the discrimination of enlightened despotism.
assignments.best_quote: she knew by instinct what sort of clay the people were made of by whom she had to work

assignments.text:
Such was the
lamentable condition, at the moment this history commences, of society
in Carlingford.
assignments.summary: The narrator summarizes the deplorable state of Carlingford society at the start of the novel, despite abundant human material available for organizing.
assignments.best_quote: Such was the lamentable condition, at the moment this history commences, of society in Carlingford.

assignments.text:
Barbara's muslin, six times
washed, was not more different from the spotless lightness of all the
draperies round her, than was her air of fright, and at the same time of
defiance, from the gay babble and pleasant looks of the group which, by
a chance combination, she seemed to form part of.
assignments.summary: The narrator starkly contrasts Barbara's six-times-washed muslin with the pristine draperies around her, and her frightened defiance with the group's gaiety.
assignments.best_quote: Barbara's muslin, six times washed, was not more different from the spotless lightness of all the draperies round her, than was her air of fright, and at the same time of defiance, from the gay babble and pleasant looks of the group

assignments.text:
"I think they are going to hang that
fellow that killed the tailor," said the amusing man; "that will stir
you up a little in Carlingford, I should suppose. It is as good as a
play for a country town.
assignments.summary: The guest mentions an upcoming execution of a man who killed a tailor and predicts it will provide entertainment for Carlingford's provincial society.
assignments.best_quote: I think they are going to hang that fellow that killed the tailor.

assignments.text:
It is a conclusion I have come to not rashly, but after many
opportunities of observing," the young man went on with solemnity; "on
the whole, my opinion is, that this is the great difference between one
portion of mankind and the other: that description of being, you may
take my word for it, has no soul."
assignments.summary: The barrister defends his position by claiming it is based on careful observation and represents the fundamental division in humanity between those with and without souls.
assignments.best_quote: this is the great difference between one portion of mankind and the other: that description of being, you may take my word for it, has no soul.

assignments.text:
Such, it is true, were the comments that were made upon the
public-spirited young woman who was doing so much for Carlingford; but
then Lucilla only shared the fate of all the great benefactors of the
world. An hour later the glories of the furniture were veiled and hidden
by the robes of a radiant flood of society, embracing all that was most
fair and all that was most distinguished in Carlingford.
assignments.summary: The narrator notes that Lucilla shares the common fate of great benefactors: criticism; an hour later the drawing-room is radiant with assembled society.
assignments.best_quote: Lucilla only shared the fate of all the great benefactors of the world

assignments.text:
He had been doing without them
for a week or two, and he had not liked it; and yet at that moment it
seemed to Mr Cavendish that he could rather be content to lose them all
at a stroke, to make it known in Carlingford that he was ruined and had
lost his fortune, than that Carlingford should find out that he was not,
after all, one of the Cavendishes, nor the person it took him for.
assignments.summary: Cavendish realizes he would rather be financially ruined than exposed as a fraud, revealing his desperate attachment to social position.
assignments.best_quote: he could rather be content to lose them all at a stroke, to make it known in Carlingford that he was ruined and had lost his fortune, than that Carlingford should find out that he was not, after all, one of the Cavendishes

assignments.text:
He
was there—he who had been so long away from Carlingford—he who had
been so deeply offended by hearing his name seriously coupled with that
of Barbara Lake—he who ought to have been anywhere in the world rather
than here upon the eve of his election, when all the world was keeping
watch over his conduct.
assignments.summary: Cavendish's presence in Barbara's parlour two days before the election represents a catastrophic breach of propriety and political judgment.
assignments.best_quote: He was there—he who had been so long away from Carlingford—he who had been so deeply offended by hearing his name seriously coupled with that of Barbara Lake—he who ought to have been anywhere in the world rather than here upon the eve of his election, when all the world was keeping watch over his conduct.

assignments.text:
He had staked his honour upon Mr Cavendish's
repentance, and here was he going back, publicly to wallow in the
mire—and it was Sunday when such a worldly subject ought not to be
permitted to enter a good man's mind, much less to be discussed and
acted upon as it ought to be if anything was to be done; for there was
little more than this sacred day remaining in which to undo the mischief
which a too great confidence in human nature had wrought.
assignments.summary: The Rector witnesses Cavendish's apparent backsliding just as Sunday prevents proper remedial action; his confidence in human nature proves false.
assignments.best_quote: here was he going back, publicly to wallow in the mire—and it was Sunday when such a worldly subject ought not to be permitted to enter a good man's mind

assignments.text:
It
was after the Archdeacon had broken down in his case against the man
whom he called an adventurer, and when Mr Cavendish felt all the
sweetness of being a member of an oligarchy, and entitled to the
sympathy and support of his order. Now he went along the same path with
his hat over his ears and his hands in his pockets, and rage and pain in
his heart.
assignments.summary: The narrator recalls how Cavendish previously basked in oligarchic privilege after the Archdeacon's courtroom defeat, contrasting with his current isolation.
assignments.best_quote: when Mr Cavendish felt all the sweetness of being a member of an oligarchy, and entitled to the sympathy and support of his order

assignments.text:
As for Mr
Cavendish himself, it began to be understood that he was with a friend
who was sick, on the Continent; and soon—for news had a wonderful
tendency to increase and grow bigger as it spread in Grange Lane—that
his friend was dying, and that a probable large increase of fortune to
the popular favourite would be the result, which was an idea that did
credit to the imagination of Carlingford.
assignments.summary: Gossip about Mr Cavendish's absence spreads wildly, with rumours growing from a friend visiting him on the Continent to the friend dying and Cavendish inheriting a fortune.
assignments.best_quote: news had a wonderful tendency to increase and grow bigger as it spread in Grange Lane

assignments.text:
"I could not think how
I was going to get her to consent," Lucilla said, "but you know she
thought I was in low spirits, the dear old soul, and that it would be a
comfort to me." Though there was often a great deal of fun at Dr
Marjoribanks's table, nothing was ever heard there to compare with the
laughter that greeted Lucilla's narrative.
assignments.summary: Lucilla reveals that she persuaded Nancy to prepare a special dish by claiming she was in low spirits, causing uproarious laughter.
assignments.best_quote: I could not think how I was going to get her to consent, but you know she thought I was in low spirits, the dear old soul, and that it would be a comfort to me

assignments.text:
The mimic was a little indolent, and would not take the trouble
to make any exertions for the good of the community, except in the
exercise of her peculiar talent, though she had been known, when
excited, to go through real fatigue for that; but she had none of the
steady force, the persevering energy—or, to sum up all in one word, the
genius—of Miss Marjoribanks, who, for her part, recognised the  use  of
such an instrument of entertainment as Mrs Woodburn possessed without
appreciating it in her own person; for Lucilla had no sense of humour,
as she candidly admitted, with that consciousness of her own faults, and
slight disposition to consider them virtues, which is common to persons
of great endowments.
assignments.summary: The narrator elaborates the fundamental difference: Mrs Woodburn relies on mimicry and entertainment talent, while Lucilla possesses steady organisational force, though Lucilla lacks humour despite her other gifts.
assignments.best_quote: Lucilla had no sense of humour, as she candidly admitted, with that consciousness of her own faults, and slight disposition to consider them virtues, which is common to persons of great endowments.

assignments.text:
Everybody was so entirely
aware of the supposed cause of the low spirits, and indeed was so
conscious of having speculated, like Nancy, upon Miss Marjoribanks's
probable demeanour at this trying moment, that the laughter was not mere
laughter, but conveyed, at the same time a confession of guilt and a
storm of applause and admiration.
assignments.summary: The narrator explains that the laughter is layered: it reveals the company's awareness of having speculated about Lucilla's distress and their amazement at her composure.
assignments.best_quote: the laughter was not mere laughter, but conveyed, at the same time a confession of guilt and a storm of applause and admiration

assignments.text:
Lucilla was, it is true, as different from her mother
as summer from winter; but Dr Marjoribanks had no means of knowing that
his daughter was only doing her duty by him in his widowhood, according
to a programme of filial devotion resolved upon, in accordance with the
best models, some days before.
assignments.summary: The narrator observes that the Doctor cannot know Lucilla's emotion is a performance, carefully choreographed according to literary models of duty.
assignments.best_quote: Dr Marjoribanks had no means of knowing that his daughter was only doing her duty by him in his widowhood, according to a programme of filial devotion resolved upon, in accordance with the best models, some days before.

assignments.text:
She even had the strength to get up to meet him, and hold
out her hands to him by way of welcome—but found herself, before she
knew how, in the arms of a man with a beard, who was so much changed in
his own person that he ventured to kiss her, which was a thing Tom
Marjoribanks, though her cousin, had never dared to do before.
assignments.summary: Lucilla rises to greet Tom but finds herself embraced by a bearded, transformed man who dares to kiss her.
assignments.best_quote: she found herself, before she knew how, in the arms of a man with a beard, who was so much changed in his own person that he ventured to kiss her, which was a thing Tom Marjoribanks, though her cousin, had never dared to do before.

assignments.text:
"Lucilla," said Tom Marjoribanks, "you know I always had a great regard
for my uncle. But it was not for him I came back. He was never half so
fond of me as I am of you. You know that as well as I do. There never
was a time that I would not have gone to the other end of the world if
you had told me; and I have done it as near as possible.
assignments.summary: Tom declares his deep regard for Lucilla has always exceeded his regard for her father, and that he left for India at her behest.
assignments.best_quote: There never was a time that I would not have gone to the other end of the world if you had told me; and I have done it as near as possible.

assignments.text:
"Him—or you!" said Lucilla, in dismay. Blunderer as he was, he had gone
direct to the very heart of the question, and it was impossible not to
tremble a little in the presence of such straightforward
clear-sightedness. Miss Marjoribanks had risen up to make her escape as
soon as it should be possible, but she was so much struck by Tom's
unlooked-for perspicuity, that she sat down again in her consternation.
assignments.summary: Lucilla is struck by Tom's unexpected perspicuity and forced to confront the central question; she sits down again, shaken by his clarity.
assignments.best_quote: Blunderer as he was, he had gone direct to the very heart of the question, and it was impossible not to tremble a little in the presence of such straightforward clear-sightedness.

assignments.text:
These words, however, were addressed to deaf ears. Tom, as was natural,
had started immediately to obey Lucilla, as he was in duty bound; and
the old Doctor looked on with a little amazement and a little amusement,
recognising, with something of the surprise which that discovery always
gives to fathers and mothers, that his visitor cared twenty times more
for what Lucilla said than for anything that his superior wisdom could
suggest.
assignments.summary: Tom immediately obeys Lucilla instead of the Doctor, demonstrating that he values Lucilla's authority more than the Doctor's.
assignments.best_quote: recognising, with something of the surprise which that discovery always gives to fathers and mothers, that his visitor cared twenty times more for what Lucilla said than for anything that his superior wisdom could suggest.

assignments.text:
When Dr
Marjoribanks had gone downstairs to resume the case which he was writing
out for the  Lancet , Lucilla passed through one of those moments of
sublime despondency which now and then try the spirits of the
benefactors of their race. A few tears came to her eyes as she reflected
upon this great problem. Without such trials genius would not fully know
itself nor be justly aware of its own strength.
assignments.summary: Lucilla is moved to tears as she contemplates the problem of her unbelieving followers; without trials genius would not know its own strength.
assignments.best_quote: Lucilla passed through one of those moments of sublime despondency which now and then try the spirits of the benefactors of their race.

assignments.text:
She had
no vocation, such as the foundress of such an establishment ought to
have, nor did she see her way to the abandonment of all projects for
herself, and that utter devotion to the cause of humanity which would be
involved in it; but yet, when a woman happens to be full of energy and
spirit, and determined that whatever she may be she shall certainly not
be a nonentity, her position is one that demands thought.
assignments.summary: Lucilla lacks true religious vocation but will not surrender personal ambition; her energetic temperament creates an unresolved ethical dilemma.
assignments.best_quote: but yet, when a woman happens to be full of energy and spirit, and determined that whatever she may be she shall certainly not be a nonentity, her position is one that demands thought

assignments.text:
People who know no better may go
away upon marriage tours, or they may fly off to foreign travel, or go
out as governesses, when all things do not go just as they wish. But as
for Miss Marjoribanks, she stood bravely at her post, and scorned to
flinch or run away. Thus commenced, amid mists of discouragement, and in
an entire absence of all that was calculated to stimulate and
exhilarate, the second grand period of Lucilla's life.
assignments.summary: While lesser people flee through marriage, travel, or governessing when disappointed, Lucilla stands firm at her post and begins her second campaign amid discouragement and without support.
assignments.best_quote: But as for Miss Marjoribanks, she stood bravely at her post, and scorned to flinch or run away. Thus commenced, amid mists of discouragement, and in an entire absence of all that was calculated to stimulate and exhilarate, the second grand period of Lucilla's life.

assignments.text:
This had been a comfort
to his mind, but it was the very falsest and most deceitful consolation. That intervening Sunday was a severer calamity for Mr Cavendish than
half a dozen ordinary days. The general excitement had risen so high,
and all the chances on both sides had been so often discussed and
debated, that something new was as water in the desert to the thirsting
constituency.
assignments.summary: The heightened election excitement makes Sunday a worse day for secrecy than any ordinary day; the news spreads like water in a desert.
assignments.best_quote: That intervening Sunday was a severer calamity for Mr Cavendish than half a dozen ordinary days.

assignments.text:
It was with this
view that Miss Marjoribanks took the step of writing to Mr Cavendish. She had written in the sacred retirement of her own maiden chamber, when
all the world was still; perhaps at the moment when General Travers was,
as he would himself have vulgarly called it, "chaffing" Cavendish about
the beautiful and disinterested friendship which united him to the young
sovereign of Grange Lane.
assignments.summary: Lucilla writes her serious note while the General speaks about Cavendish and her, creating ironic contrast between her agency and male gossip.
assignments.best_quote: She had written in the sacred retirement of her own maiden chamber, when all the world was still; perhaps at the moment when General Travers was, as he would himself have vulgarly called it, "chaffing" Cavendish about the beautiful and disinterested friendship which united him to the young sovereign of Grange Lane

assignments.text:
When he was
coming out of the house, as a matter of course, he met with the chief of
his Dissenting supporters, accompanied (for Mr Bury, as has been said,
was very Low-Church, and loved, wherever he could do it, to work in
unison with his Dissenting brethren) by the Rector's churchwarden, both
of whom stopped with a curiously critical air to speak to the Candidate,
who had to be every man's friend for the time being.
assignments.summary: Cavendish encounters his key supporters leaving the Lake house, and their critical looks suggest they have observed and judged his visit.
